title: Priming of Wheat Seeds with Functionalized Chitosan Aspartate Nanoparticles
content: A new type of chitosan nanoparticles was obtained by counter ionic association of chitosan macromolecular chains with L- and D-aspartic acid and stabilized with a glycerohydrogel polysiloxane coating based on silicon tetraglycerolate. These are spherical nanoparticles with an average diameter of 100–150 nm and a relatively narrow size distribution. An assessment of the effect of chitosan nanoparticles on the early stages of wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) development and on the rhizosphere soil microbiome under optimal and stress conditions revealed that maximum growth-promoting activity was observed when the nanoparticle concentration in the dispersion was reduced to 0.0003 g/dL. The growth-promoting activity manifested by stimulation of root growth and biomass accumulation not only under conditions of high water availability in the soil but also under water scarcity. Stimulation of the synthesis of photosynthetic pigments and an increase in the activity of antioxidant enzymes were observed. A comparison of the effects of chitosan L- and D-aspartate demonstrates the advantage of the presence of the L-stereoisomer of aspartic acid in the nanostructured salt complex. The data indicate that shell-coated chitosan aspartate nanoparticles can be used in agrobiotechnology for seed priming to stimulate of wheat plant growth.
